one_line: Second Sikh Guru who codified and spread the Gurmukhi script and nurtured disciplined community life at Khadur Sahib.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s to early 50s, medium height, gently broad-shouldered but not muscular, with a calm, grounded posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with a slightly broad forehead, warm wheatish Punjabi complexion, straight nose, gentle but focused almond-shaped brown eyes, neatly kept medium-length beard that tapers softly, and a serene default expression conveying quiet determination and compassion.
appearance.hair: Hair kept fully covered under a neatly tied, medium-height white turban (dastar) with smooth wraps and a slight ridge at the front; no ornamentation, only a simple, clean fold line running across the forehead.
appearance.costume: A long, knee-length off-white cotton kurta with straight sleeves and a modest round neckline, worn over a slightly looser light-cream churidar pajama; a plain light-ochre shawl (chadar) draped from the left shoulder across the torso and around the back, its end falling over the right forearm; simple brown leather sandals, and a slim cloth kamarband under the shawl implied at the waist; fabrics look handspun and slightly textured, with no embroidery or rich decoration, reflecting humility and early 16th-century rural Punjab.
appearance.signature: A bound palm-leaf or early paper pothi (manuscript book) with a simple brown cover and a visible wooden writing board tucked under his left arm, accompanied by a reed pen held lightly in his right hand, symbolizing his role in codifying and teaching Gurmukhi.

ref_desc: Guru Angad appears as a calm, middle-aged Sikh man with a wheatish oval face, white turban, neatly tapered beard, off-white kurta, light-cream churidar, light-ochre shawl, brown sandals, and carrying a simple brown pothi with a wooden writing board and reed pen in warm neutral tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Guru Angad as a dignified, historically grounded early-16th-century Sikh Guru from rural Punjab: a calm middle-aged man with an oval wheatish face, gentle brown eyes, and a neatly kept medium-length beard that tapers softly; his hair is fully covered by a smooth, medium-height white turban with clean, simple wraps and no ornaments. He wears a knee-length off-white cotton kurta with straight sleeves and a modest round neckline, over a light-cream churidar pajama that gathers subtly at the ankles, and plain brown leather sandals on his feet. A light-ochre shawl (chadar) is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back, with one end falling over his right forearm, fabrics looking handspun, slightly textured, and undecorated to emphasize humility and simplicity. Show him holding a bound brown pothi (manuscript book) and a flat wooden writing board tucked under his left arm, while his right hand gently holds a reed pen, all in warm neutral browns and creams; keep the palette to off-white, light cream, light ochre, warm brown, and soft white, and present him from multiple angles in consistent costume and colours to emphasize his role as a serene teacher and codifier of the Gurmukhi script.
